solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Knitter's beginning to replace front of pullover with simple woollen fabric

indicators.note: one letter is swapped in for the opening letter of the following word, leaving the rest intact
the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one letter is kept

parts.note: opening letter of the knitter
a jersey is a knitted pullover; its J is swapped for K
mere as in a mere child: simple, nothing more

explanation.surface: A knitting instruction: start by replacing the front panel of a sweater with plain wool cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap lands on a real word first: kersey is itself a coarse ribbed cloth, and the longer fabric grew from its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerseymere is a fine twilled cloth, a plain material once used for trousers and waistcoats.

clue.text: Vancouver islanders with regular appearances in skiwear knit until start of summer

indicators.note: letters that turn up at regular intervals are every second one of the string that follows

parts.note: the even-placed letters of these three words

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: first letter of summer

explanation.surface: Islanders off Canada's west coast are spotted now and then in ski clothing knitted for winter.
explanation.walkthrough: The S on the end makes the people plural.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kwakiutl are a First Nations people of northern Vancouver Island and the nearby British Columbia coast.

clue.text: Tool for scraping base element from upper atmosphere containing chlorine monoxide

indicators.note: one piece holds the others inside it
in a down clue the base of a word is its bottom, final letter

parts.note: last letter of upper
air is the atmosphere
the chemical symbol for chlorine
mono-oxide: a single O, the symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A chemistry-lab scraper for collecting a base element from the upper atmosphere, laced with chlorine monoxide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upper atmosphere' reads as one phrase, but upper only lends its final letter; in a down clue the base is the bottom of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A racloir is a prehistoric flint scraper, the stone tool archaeologists name for scraping hides.

clue.text: Course deviation crossing road with old rod as a measure

indicators.note: a path crossing something straddles it, so one piece sits across the other and encloses it

parts.note: a yaw is a swing off course by a ship or aircraft
standard abbreviation of road
and adds one thing with another

explanation.surface: A ship veers off course across a road while carrying an old surveying rod.
explanation.walkthrough: Course deviation sounds like a golf or race-track error, but it is the nautical and aviation term for swinging off heading.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardwand is the archaic name for a yardstick, a rod exactly one yard long used for measuring cloth.

clue.text: Hesitant words about unknown quantity that is unable to decide eg Nero's origin story?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a loose, playful definition of a novel of upbringing

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps the next three

parts.note: er is the word of hesitation; several of them
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z
i.e., Latin id est, that is
a hung jury cannot reach a verdict
Nero was a Roman emperor, one example of a Roman

explanation.surface: Stammered remarks about some indecisive mystery quantity, framed as the tale of how Nero came to be.
explanation.walkthrough: Erziehungsroman is German for a novel of upbringing, a near relative of the Bildungsroman; the hesitation word is pluralised and opens around the middle pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel tracing a hero's upbringing and education is literally the story of how that character originated.

clue.text: Turtles get up to welcome brother Donatello at first

indicators.note: welcoming guests means taking them in, so one piece goes inside the other
in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the word is turned round

parts.note: to get it is to see it, understand
both are exclamations of surprise: Oh brother! Oh my!

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the name is used

parts.note: first letter of the name

explanation.surface: The Ninja Turtles rise to greet their brother Donatello first.
explanation.walkthrough: Donatello is one of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, the surface's bait. Brother as an exclamation matches MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Emydes is the plural of emys, a genus name used for freshwater terrapins and pond tortoises.

clue.text: Prison bunk, both short and sweet, in Invercargill

indicators.note: each of the two words is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: jug is slang for prison
a bunk is a bed

explanation.surface: A jail bed in a New Zealand town that is both cramped and cosy.
explanation.walkthrough: Invercargill is a New Zealand city, flagging a New Zealand word.
explanation.definitionFit: In New Zealand and Australia a jube is a chewy jelly sweet, short for jujube.

clue.text: States, after the writer in French book, tree height in Morocco

indicators.note: after places the first named piece behind everything that follows it in the clue

parts.note: the French for I, the writer referring to themselves
standard abbreviation of book
a common tree
the United States

explanation.surface: Listing the States after a French author's book and the height of a tree in Morocco.
explanation.definitionFit: Jebel Musa is a mountain on the Moroccan side of the Strait of Gibraltar, one of the Pillars of Hercules.

clue.text: Water carrier wanting silence during work meeting

indicators.note: something said during an event happens inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a bee is a gathering for shared work, like a quilting bee
hist is a call for silence, said by someone wanting quiet

explanation.surface: Someone at an office meeting is short on quiet and wants the water jug passed along.
explanation.definitionFit: A bhistee was an Indian servant who fetched and carried water in a leather bag.

clue.text: Pen once possessed by Mozart, a classicist recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters run backwards
what is possessed by these words is held within their letters

parts.note: a run straddling these words

explanation.surface: A classical scholar remembers a fountain pen that Mozart owned.
explanation.walkthrough: Pen means prison, and 'once' points to a closed one: the island jail in San Francisco Bay.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcatraz was a federal prison until 1963, so it is a former penitentiary, a pen in slang.

clue.text: Aussie nipper's reduced offer accepted by auction site in turn

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken in, so it goes inside the other piece
turned round, the word reads from right to left

parts.note: eBay, the online auction site

indicators.note: something reduced is cut down, losing its last letter

parts.note: a bid is an offer at auction; it loses its D

explanation.surface: An Australian child has a lowered bid taken by an auction website.
explanation.walkthrough: Nipper means a pincered creature here, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A yabbie is a small Australian freshwater crayfish, a creature with nipping claws.

clue.text: Revered image of king in part of compound

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: an ion is a charged part of an ionic compound
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A sacred picture of a king set into part of a building complex.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikon is a variant spelling of icon, a venerated religious picture in Orthodox churches.

clue.text: Drug suitably absorbed by colourless mineral in kidney stones

indicators.note: what is absorbed is soaked up inside, so these pieces go within the other

parts.note: white is colourless
E is ecstasy
well as in done well, suitably

explanation.surface: A drug duly absorbed by a pale mineral that forms kidney stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Whewellite is calcium oxalate monohydrate, the crystal that makes up most human kidney stones.

clue.text: Mount soldiers to front corporation's war machine

indicators.note: the earlier pieces stand at the front, ahead of the one named after

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill
soldiers are men in the ranks
corporation is old slang for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: Put troops on horseback to lead a company's military hardware.
explanation.walkthrough: Mount looks like a verb and corporation like a company; they are a hill and a belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentum was an ancient Roman siege engine, a catapult powered by twisted ropes.

clue.text: Mother and Mike selfishly keep little fish

parts.note: British for mom
mike is a microphone, also written mic
to hog is to keep for oneself

explanation.surface: A mother and someone called Mike greedily guard a small fish for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike looks like a name or the NATO letter M, but here it is a microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: The mummichog is a small killifish of North American Atlantic coastal marshes.

clue.text: Possibly eight billion dried berries

definitions.note: plural in the clue; cubeb is used as a mass noun for the spice

parts.note: eight is two cubed, so one example of a cube number
B is the abbreviation for billion

explanation.surface: Maybe eight billion berries have been dried.
explanation.walkthrough: Eight looks like a count with billion; it is a cube number, and billion gives one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubeb is the dried unripe fruit of a Javanese pepper, sold as a spice.

clue.text: Gobbledygook in an attempt to stop airline bankruptcy

parts.note: British Airways

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a hole, so this piece is put inside the next

parts.note: financial ruin
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: Corporate jargon from a rescue bid meant to save a carrier from going bust.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the attempt stops the bankruptcy and the airline comes first: BA, then RUIN holding A GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Baragouin is a French-derived word for unintelligible jargon or gibberish.

clue.text: Conformity of rating on island nightclub activity

parts.note: an AB, able seaman, is a naval rating
standard abbreviation of island
what people do at a nightclub

explanation.surface: A sailor on an island club fitting in with the dancefloor crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Rating sounds like a score; in the Royal Navy it is an ordinary sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Abidance by rules means compliance with them, the act of keeping to an agreement.

clue.text: Teacher's whiskey drunk by Laplander

indicators.note: what is drunk goes inside the drinker

parts.note: the Sami are the people of Lapland
whiskey is W in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: The schoolteacher's whiskey gets drunk by a reindeer herder from Lapland.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher, a title of respect for a master.

clue.text: Local maker of saddles shortened crop and upped power unit

indicators.note: shortened means cut, losing the last letter

parts.note: a riding crop is a short whip

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent upwards so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: the watt is the SI unit of power

explanation.surface: A village saddler trims a riding crop and fixes up an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: Local signals a dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Whittaw is a dialect word for a saddler or harness-maker, one who works white leather.

clue.text: Moth circles round Washington's chopper

indicators.note: to circle something is to go all the way round it

parts.note: the egger, or eggar, is a large brown moth
a police officer's round is a beat

explanation.surface: A moth flies circles round the first president's axe.
explanation.walkthrough: Washington stands for American usage; chopper suggests the cherry-tree hatchet.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang an eggbeater is a helicopter, from the whirring of its rotor.

clue.text: European tug, craft from the south, shows small forest animal

indicators.note: read from the south in a down clue means from the bottom upwards

parts.note: standard abbreviation
to lug is to tug or haul
art is craft, skill

explanation.surface: A European tugboat and another vessel heading north turn out to carry a small woodland creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Tug and craft look like boats; they are a verb and a skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragule is a chevrotain or mouse deer, a tiny hoofed mammal of tropical forest.

clue.text: Choice to get width of printing in completely filled space

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a plum job is a choice one
an en is a printer's unit of width

explanation.surface: A print shop picks a setting that fills a page edge to edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A plenum is space entirely occupied by matter, the opposite of a vacuum.

clue.text: Rough core from quarry in excavation is reviewed to find tree-like fossil

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the rest
viewed back, so read in the opposite direction

parts.note: an archaeological dig
taken as written
feeling rough is feeling ill

indicators.note: the core of a word is its middle, so only the centre letters are kept

parts.note: the middle two of six letters

explanation.surface: A rough core from a quarry is studied again at a dig and turns out to be a fossil tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Rough here means unwell, not coarse; the two middle letters of quarry join it inside the turned-round dig and is.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigillaria was a giant tree-like club moss of the coal age; a sigillarid is a fossil of that group.

clue.text: Half-finished jumper with a pouch that's warm to sleep on

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for the noun

indicators.note: only half of the word is completed, so the second half is dropped

parts.note: the kangaroo jumps and carries its young in a pouch

explanation.surface: A half-knitted sweater with a front pocket that will keep you warm in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumper is a British word for a sweater, which the pouch makes look like a kangaroo-pocket top.
explanation.definitionFit: A kang is a heated brick platform used as a bed in northern China.

clue.text: Haunt a degenerate in a religious state?

definitions.note: a phrase describing the person rather than a noun; the question mark admits it

indicators.note: to degenerate is to fall apart, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: the six letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Torment a fallen sinner who is in a state of religious devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: State is literal: Utah, the US state settled by Mormons.
explanation.definitionFit: A Utahan is a native of Utah, a state famous as the home of the Mormon church.

clue.text: A loss nearly burying quiet British guesthouse

indicators.note: to bury is to put inside, so the next pieces go within
nearly all of the word means stopping one letter short

parts.note: a minus is a loss or deficit; it drops its S
sh is a call for quiet
the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A financial hit very nearly sinks a quiet British B&B.
explanation.definitionFit: A minshuku is a family-run Japanese bed-and-breakfast, a modest inn in a private home.

clue.text: Around noon, this nautical pulley is to be strung up

indicators.note: the clue runs backwards: put round one letter, the answer makes a longer word, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: to swing is to be hanged
N is noon, the letter for midday

explanation.surface: At midday, a ship's block and tackle is due to be hoisted.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue builds a different word from the answer: this answer placed round N becomes SWING. Strung up means hanged, not hoisted.
explanation.definitionFit: On ships a swig is a tackle whose ropes are not parallel, a kind of hauling block.

clue.text: Misheard words about 60 Minutes in Minnesota

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the other

parts.note: the postal abbreviation for Minnesota
on as in a talk on birds, about
sixty minutes of arc make one degree

explanation.surface: A garbled report about the TV news show 60 Minutes, filmed in Minnesota.
explanation.walkthrough: 60 Minutes looks like the CBS programme or an hour; it is an angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A mondegreen is a misinterpreted phrase, especially a misheard song lyric, named from 'laid him on the green'.
